newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK exchange seeks smooth Beijing Enterprises issue.
newsitem.headline: HK exchange seeks smooth Beijing Enterprises issue.

text.p: The Hong Kong stock exchange said on Thursday it told Peregrine Capital Ltd it was concerned about an orderly market in the face of feverish demand for Beijing Enterprises Holdings Ltd's share offering.
Peregrine Capital is joint global coordinator of the issue with Morgan Stanley Asia Ltd.
"In order to ensure an orderly market, we reminded (Peregrine) that they should make sure that everything goes all right," a stock exchange spokesman told Reuters.
He said Peregrine officials met exchange chief executive Alec Tsui and head of the listing division Lawrence Fok on Wednesday.
He declined to comment on reports that stock exchange officials had met with Beijing Enterprises management.
Beijing Enterprises, controlled by the Beijing municipal government, is offering 150 million shares in a global initial public offering (IPO) at HK$12.48 per share.
Ten percent of the issue is being offered to the Hong Kong public and 90 percent in an international placement.
The exchange wanted to make sure the IPO would run smoothly, the spokesman said, adding it would closely monitor the situation until the close of the offer on Friday.
He said the exchange was looking at the market reaction and the availability of application forms for the new issue.
Banks ran out of application forms for the second day in a row on Wednesday as retail investors and punters clambered to apply for the shares, which are trading at huge premiums in the grey market.
Peregrine said on Wednesday it had asked for another 200,000 forms to be printed, bringing the total to more than one million.
Brokers said the grey market price was nearly three times the issue price at about HK$37. Dealing in the shares is due to begin on May 29.
Beijing Enterprises is the primary commercial vehicle for the Beijing municipal government to access international markets for capital, technology and management expertise.
The conglomerate is involved in retailing, infrastructure, hotel services and the high-tech industry.
